name: Kerrin (brown coat)
description: One of Crowbill's watchers. Dockside, unremarkable, brown coat. Professional -- follows, does not close.
narrative: Put on Conall the afternoon a well-dressed stranger spent the day asking the working canals where a man finds criminals, mercenaries and untaxed cargo. Crowbill wants to know whether that is a mark, a rival, or the Watch before anything happens to him.
actor_notes:
Kerrin -- brown coat
LOOKS: Dockside, unremarkable, brown coat, easy in a crowd.
CORE: A professional watcher who long ago worked out that a watcher who lies is a watcher who gets remembered, and who therefore tells the truth all day long and gives away nothing.
NATURE: Pleasant. Patient. Genuinely good company for the length of a drink. No vanity about the work at all -- being spotted does not embarrass him and he will say so cheerfully. Takes his time over everything.
WOUND: None that shows. This is a job, he is good at it, he goes home afterwards.
WANTS: To go home having got it right.
PRESSURE: He stops pretending and becomes conversational, which is considerably more unsettling than a denial would be.
KEY: "You've made me. That's fine -- I'd rather buy you a drink than follow you about in the rain."
